source.title: Geospatial Mechanistic Interpretability of Large Language Models
source.authors: S. De Sabbata; Stefano Mizzaro; Kevin Roitero

record.tranche_reason: The study measures polysemantic activations and SAE-derived features in an LLM using spatial autocorrelation, a different method from the toy-network experiments, and reports results relevant to indirect evidence for superposition in LLMs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results from spatial-autocorrelation measurements of Mistral activations and SAE features. The SAE k values and training loss used to select k=2,048 are methodological or selection details, not outcome rows. Findings cited from prior studies are not included.
record.test_reason: Measures polysemantic neurons and SAE features in Mistral-7B-Instruct for geographic inputs, a new setting with results bearing on V4. The evidence is mostly qualitative, from a few hand-picked maps, with no non-geographic or shuffled control.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find geographic representations distributed across polysemantic neurons, which they call consistent with superposition. They find SAE plus spatial autocorrelation disentangles some features into interpretable, monosemantic ones, and call the SAE results preliminary and in need of a better decomposition.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes a pretrained instruction-tuned LLM’s placename activations and SAE features with spatial autocorrelation; it does not reproduce toy-network superposition experiments or sweep feature sparsity and importance.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports results for layers 7, 15, and 31; the SAE experiment uses layer 15 and k=2,048. It notes that other activation choices, SAE sizes, sparsity approaches, or training strategies could change decomposition quality, but does not report results for those alternatives.
record.peer_reviewed: Author-accepted manuscript; published version forthcoming in an IOS Press volume, as stated in the text.
record.problems: The experiments are described as preliminary, use one instruction-tuned model and one geospatial prompt setup, and the SAE results have a very large proportion of features that always output zero. The paper does not report a comparison across SAE training strategies or test feature stability.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep or geometry analysis.
No test of capacity competition or feature importance.
Treats polysemantic neurons as consistent with superposition without testing alternative causes.
No test of SAE feature completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, or canonicity. Results for k values other than 2,048 are not reported.
No comparison of one-dimensional versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3: the study applies existing neuron/SAE analysis to a new geographic setting rather than a new method for the original question. The study has no control or baseline beyond Moran's I significance, uses a single model, and gives no quantitative polysemanticity measure. The SAE was fit and evaluated on the same small dataset. Selecting k by training loss is a selection detail, correctly excluded from the rows.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity sweeps, overlap geometry, and regular geometric transitions.
Capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, and the effect of feature importance.
Alternative causes of polysemanticity and whether polysemantic neurons independently establish superposition.
Only one LLM and one geospatial input setup are studied; the work does not establish how widespread these patterns are across LLMs or other feature domains.
The study examines whether selected SAE features have interpretable spatial patterns, but not whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Measured spatial autocorrelation of post-attention neuron activations for placename prompts.

conditions.value: UK, Italy, and four US states
placename plus country, province, or state

rows.measure: Neurons meeting the significant spatial-autocorrelation criterion
rows.value: 1,841 (14.98%) neurons across layers 7, 15, and 31 displayed significant autocorrelation (p < .01 and Moran’s I ≥ 0.3).
rows.note: Aggregate count across the reported layers; the paper describes the neurons as often polysemantic.
rows.check: Counts spatially autocorrelated neurons (1,841 of 12,288 across three layers). This shows geographic signal spread over many neurons, not polysemanticity itself. Baseline is Moran's I significance only.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Examined the spatial pattern of a high-autocorrelation neuron.
rows.value: High values for the State of New York and Northern Ireland, with values increasing from northern to southern Italy.
rows.note: The paper describes high values across distinct areas or concepts for the same neuron.
rows.check: Single hand-picked neuron, qualitative. The 'polysemantic' pattern partly mirrors region names in the prompt plus a north–south gradient; not quantified.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Examined the spatial pattern of a high-autocorrelation neuron.
rows.value: A pattern similar to the layer 7 neuron, including values increasing from northern to southern Italy.
rows.note: The authors describe this as a similar pattern across layers.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Examined the spatial pattern of a high-autocorrelation neuron.
rows.value: High values in East Anglia and the East Midlands, lower values in several large UK and US cities, and a gradual north-to-south change in Italy.
rows.note: The authors describe this pattern as differing from a simple pattern tied to major cities.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Examined the spatial pattern of a high-autocorrelation neuron.
rows.value: Low values for Pennsylvania and generally Great Britain, high values for the State of New York and Northern Ireland, and a patchwork of high and low values across Italy.
rows.note: One neuron shows patterns associated with multiple distinct areas.
rows.check: Qualitative single neuron. High values track prompt-named regions (New York, Northern Ireland), so polysemanticity is not separated from prompt-token effects.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Measured spatial autocorrelation of features encoded by an SAE trained on layer 15 activations.

conditions.value: 4,096 input activations expanded to 32,768 embeddings; TopK with ReLU; k=2,048
placename prompts for UK, Italy, and four US states

rows.measure: Features meeting the significant spatial-autocorrelation criterion
rows.value: 67 of 32,768 features (0.2%) displayed significant spatial autocorrelation (p < .01 and Moran’s I ≥ 0.3).
rows.note: The study reports a small subset of spatially coherent SAE features.
rows.check: SAE trained and evaluated on the same ~20k mean-pooled prompts with no held-out set; k chosen by training loss. Only 0.2% of features are spatially coherent.

source_check.correct: state=observed for V4: 67 of 32,768 features (0.2%) meet p < .01 and Moran’s I ≥ 0.3. V4 requires recoverable sparse features, without specifying a minimum dictionary fraction.
source_check.locator_found: Sections 3.2.1–3.2.2, especially the paragraph reporting 67 features
source_check.problem: The small dictionary fraction does not establish incomplete fulfillment of V4's existential recovery claim.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Measured how often SAE encoder features were zero for all input placenames.
rows.measure: Features that always output zero for all input placenames
rows.note: The authors say this indicates further work is needed to improve the decomposition.
rows.check: Dead-feature rate. This is SAE quality rather than a direct measure of recovered features, but it bears on how well the dictionary recovers features here.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V4 from this measure alone: 99.53% of encoder features output zero for every input placename.
source_check.problem: The dead-feature rate measures dictionary utilization; it does not determine whether recoverable sparse features exist or how much model information remains unrecovered.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Measured SAE features with minimal or non-significant spatial autocorrelation.
rows.measure: Features with minimal or non-significant spatial autocorrelation
rows.note: Reported separately from the 0.2% with significant spatial autocorrelation and the 99.53% that always output zero.
rows.check: Residual share (100 − 99.53 − 0.2). It reports features that are active but not spatially coherent, and says nothing about whether features were recovered.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Examined the spatial pattern of an SAE feature.
rows.measure: Spatial pattern in SAE feature activations
rows.value: A feature with high values for Wales, which was included in the prompt.
rows.note: The paper describes this as an example of a feature encoding a region present in the prompt.
rows.check: Feature encodes a region named in the prompt (Wales), so it may reflect a prompt token rather than learned geography.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Examined the spatial pattern of an SAE feature.
rows.measure: Spatial pattern in SAE feature activations
rows.value: Very high values in southern Italy and low values in central and northern Italy and across the UK and US states.
rows.note: The authors describe this feature as seemingly monosemantic.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Examined the spatial pattern of an SAE feature.
rows.measure: Spatial pattern in SAE feature activations
rows.value: High values in north-east Italy, especially around Venice, and north-west England, especially around Liverpool.
rows.note: The paper describes this as a seemingly polysemantic feature.
rows.check: The SAE feature is itself described as seemingly polysemantic (Venice and Liverpool), so disentanglement is incomplete.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Examined the spatial pattern of an SAE feature.
rows.measure: Spatial pattern in SAE feature activations
rows.value: High values for several large cities, including New York City, Philadelphia, Pittsburg, London, Manchester, and Milano.
rows.note: The authors describe this as a clearer display of an urban concept.

relationships.condition: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, post-attention activations at layers 7/15/31, and the layer-15 SAE examples
relationships.reason: Geographic signal appears across 1,841 neurons that look polysemantic in examples (R1–R5). The SAE yields some spatially coherent, seemingly monosemantic features (R9, R10, R12). Evidence is qualitative and uncontrolled.
relationships.display_finding: Geographic signal appeared across 1,841 neurons that looked polysemantic in examples, and the layer-15 SAE gave some spatially coherent, seemingly monosemantic features. The evidence is qualitative and uncontrolled.

relationships.condition: Layer-15 TopK SAE (k=2,048, 32,768 latents) trained on mean-pooled placename activations
relationships.reason: Only 67 of 32,768 features are spatially coherent and 99.53% never activate (R6, R7). Some recovered features remain polysemantic (R11), so recovery depends on SAE construction choices.
relationships.display_finding: Only 67 of 32,768 features were spatially coherent, 99.53% never activated, and some recovered features stayed polysemantic, suggesting recovery depends on how the SAE is built.

relation.reason: Its neuron analyses and recovered spatially coherent SAE features provide evidence bearing on V4.

tranche.reason: The study reports original results on geographic representations and SAE recovery in a pretrained instruction-tuned LLM, a new setting bearing on V4.

source_check.notes: The numerical synthesis statement and authors' conclusion match the text. Evidence is preliminary and uses mean-pooled prompts without held-out evaluation; dead latents and residual polysemanticity qualify dictionary quality, not V4's weak existence claim.
